## Hybrid Retrieval

Hybrid retrieval combines **sparse lexical search** (e.g. BM25) with **dense vector search**, then merges the two ranked result sets—often via reciprocal rank fusion—to capture both exact term matches and semantic similarity.

This pattern excels on queries mixing:
- Rare identifiers (error codes, product SKUs) — where sparse methods excel
- Natural language intent — where dense semantic methods excel

Hybrid retrieval consistently outperforms either method alone and has become the default retrieval pattern in production RAG systems.

### Merging Strategies

**Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF)** is the standard approach for combining sparse and dense results into a unified ranked set.
